Lessons.Title: Estimating a Population Mean
ExplanationParagraphs: Source-aligned goals: Determine (in writing) an estimate for the population mean with a margin of error using sample means from random samples.

A random sample mean estimates the population mean. An approximate 95% interval may use sample mean ±2s/sqrt(n) when conditions are met; genuine interpretation requires a random sample and attention to outliers.

Source activity 12.1: Rolling Distribution: In the next activity, you will roll a standard number cube 35 times. Draw a dot plot that shows the distribution of values you might expect for the rolls. Explain your reasoning. If you rolled the number cube one million times and found the mean of all the values, what do you expect for the mean? Explain your reasoning. Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Practice Problem 1: Technology required The mean amount spent on daycare yearly by random samples of 10 families are listed. Use the values to estimate the mean amount spent on daycare yearly for the population, and provide a margin of error (round to the nearest dollar). Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 2: Technology required 25 random samples of 30 people each were measured for their daily water usage. The mean for each sample is included in the dot plot. Use the values to estimate the mean water usage for the population. What is the margin of error for this estimate based on these values? Practice Problem 3: Select all of the values for the population mean that would be plausible based on an estimate of 105 cm with a margin of error of 21 cm. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 4: A normal curve with a mean of 70 and a standard deviation of 20 is shown. Shade the region under the curve between the mean and one standard deviation greater than the mean. How much of the data falls within the shaded region? Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
